title: Arbitrary CPI Cross Program Invocation Attack
text:
Arbitrary CPI (Cross Program Invocation) Vulnerability

Description:
When a program accepts an arbitrary program account and invokes it without
validation, an attacker can pass a malicious program that steals funds or
corrupts state.

Vulnerable pattern:
```rust
pub fn cpi_transfer(ctx: Context<CpiTransfer>, amount: u64) -> Result<()> {
    let ix = transfer(
        ctx.accounts.token_program.key,  // Not validated!
        ctx.accounts.from.key,
        ctx.accounts.to.key,
        ctx.accounts.authority.key,
        &[],
        amount,
    )?;
    invoke(&ix, &[...])?;
    Ok(())
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct CpiTransfer<'info> {
    token_program: AccountInfo<'info>,  // Any program accepted!
}
```

Secure pattern:
```rust
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct CpiTransfer<'info> {
    #[account(address = spl_token::ID)]  // Validate program address
    token_program: Program<'info, Token>,
}
```

Or manually:
```rust
require!(
    ctx.accounts.token_program.key() == &spl_token::ID,
    ErrorCode::InvalidProgram
);
```

Detection AST pattern: AccountInfo for program fields without address constraint.
Detection CFG pattern: invoke() or invoke_signed() without program key check.
Source: Sealevel Attacks #5, Neodyme Common Pitfalls
